rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes adding ~5 at% V to NbMoTaW, while the paper added 20 at% Re. Both are compositional modifications of the same base alloy, but the specific element and amount differ.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions room-temperature mechanical tests, 1600 °C tests, and standardized irradiation, whereas the paper used room-temperature magnetron sputtering, room-temperature nanoindentation/micropillar compression, and 120 keV He2+ irradiation at room temperature. The hypothesis does not specify the paper's film form, deposition method, or irradiation conditions.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes lowering the Peierls barrier and promoting slip systems for ductility, while the paper's mechanism relies on grain refinement, lattice distortion, excess free volume, and amorphous grain-boundary regions acting as defect sinks to suppress He-bubble growth and embrittlement. These are different classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved room-temperature ductility, maintained high-temperature performance, and unchanged irradiation resistance. The paper's outcome is improved He-irradiation resistance (less hardening, less embrittlement) at room temperature, with no high-temperature testing. The predicted property (irradiation resistance) and direction (improvement) align, but the hypothesis adds ductility and high-temperature performance not measured in the paper.
